clue.text: As printed, this could make propane

parts.note: the clue's own letters ask what, rearranged, would give the word propane: the two-word phrase meaning in written form does exactly that

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: a printed formula that could, in principle, be used to make the gas propane.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer is the fodder, and propane is what its letters make when rearranged; 'could make' is the anagram signal read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set down in writing or print is said to exist only in that written form, an idiom for printed.

clue.text: Boring entrepreneurs taking time away from industry workers

indicators.note: taking something out of a group of words removes it, here working with away from
away from says the time abbreviation leaves the word built from industry and workers

parts.note: industry means hard work, toil
workers are men in the old crossword sense of hands or staff

explanation.surface: Dull businessmen take time off from the labourers who work for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling: these entrepreneurs bore for crude.
explanation.definitionFit: People in the petroleum business make their fortunes by drilling, or boring, wells.

clue.text: Ballerina shaking bottom, one who induced drooling

indicators.note: shaking off its bottom letter means the last letter of the dancer's name is lost

parts.note: Anna Pavlova was a famous Russian ballerina

explanation.surface: A dancer wiggles her behind and leaves an onlooker slavering.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the bottom is the last letter, shaken off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian physiologist conditioned dogs to salivate at a signal that food was coming.

clue.text: Model receiving complaint to consider retiring after hostilities ended

indicators.note: receiving means the word for model takes in the ailment

parts.note: to model is to pose
a complaint is an illness; TB is tuberculosis

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for consider is read backwards

parts.note: to consider is to mull over

explanation.surface: A model with a grievance thinks about leaving the profession once the fighting stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is the disease TB, a common crossword stand-in for an illness; 'after hostilities ended' is Latin-flavoured usage for postwar.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for after the war, used especially of the period following the American Civil War.

clue.text: Use oven or pan

definitions.meaning: to cook meat in dry heat in an oven
to pan is to criticise severely, like a scathing review

explanation.surface: A cook choosing between the oven and a frying pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like a kitchen noun; it is the verb for slating a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking in an oven is one sense; a harsh critique, giving someone a grilling, is the other.

clue.text: See 16
US shooter backing renegade, rogue nation

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word for renegade is reversed

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or deserter

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means behaving wildly, so the letters of nation run amok

explanation.surface: An American gunman supporting a traitor and a rogue state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' suggests a gunman, but this one shoots films: Quentin Tarantino, the US director.
explanation.definitionFit: A film director shoots movies, so the American filmmaker is a shooter in the camera sense.

clue.text: Constituent's texting: "You idiot!"

parts.note: in texting shorthand, you is written as the single letter U
a nit, short for nitwit, is an idiot

explanation.surface: An MP's constituent sends an abusive text message calling them an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Texting' tells you to write 'You' the way a text message would.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is one component or element of a larger whole, as a constituent is.

clue.text: Daughter getting on alcohol's in depressed state

parts.note: getting on means ageing, old
rum is alcohol; rum's reads as RUMS

explanation.surface: A daughter growing older turns to drink and becomes depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums means feeling low and listless, named after the windless calm zone near the equator.

clue.text: Game to defraud, pocketing pounds in crooked stocktaking

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: pocketing means the swindle takes the pounds inside it

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick that defrauds
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A rigged game in which a fraudster pockets cash by fiddling the stock count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocktaking' is not counting inventory: the stock is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing cattle or horses is livestock theft, a dishonest way of taking stock.

clue.text: Corbyn's defeated after nothing succeeded in funny drama

indicators.note: after places the defeat part behind the nothing-and-succeeded opening

parts.note: love means zero, nothing, as in tennis scores
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
Jeremy Corbyn led the UK Labour Party, so Corbyn's is Labour's
defeated means lost

explanation.surface: A Labour leader beaten after early success at nothing, played as farce.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn led Britain's Labour Party in its 2019 election defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's early comedy about four young men forswearing women is an example of a funny play.

clue.text: Broadcast US comic's takeoffs from here

parts.note: to air is to broadcast
W.C. Fields was a US comedian; the possessive merely joins

explanation.surface: Radio airs a US comedian's impressions, his takeoffs of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takeoffs' looks like comic impressions, following 'comic's'; it is planes leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft depart from landing grounds, so these are the places where flights take off.

clue.text: Brexit not a disaster? It's very costly

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A political argument: Brexit may not be a catastrophe, but it is very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant prices are excessive, far beyond reasonable, so very costly.

clue.text: Viva the foreign king, over from the east!

indicators.note: in an across clue, going from the east means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: la is French for the
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cheer of Long live the foreign king, sent over from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viva' looks like a cheer; it is the noun for a spoken examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva voce examination is a spoken test, the same as an oral.

clue.text: Day to clear out town for the better

parts.note: MON is short for Monday

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of to clear are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants a day to clear the town out, to make things better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' sounds like bettor, one who bets: the definition is a gamblers' town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monaco resort is famed for its casino, a destination for gamblers.

clue.text: Both parents in lounge at home, or one helping kids outside

parts.note: to loll is to lounge about

indicators.note: in says both parents sit inside the word for at home

parts.note: in means at home
pop and ma, father and mother

explanation.surface: Mum and dad lounge at home, or one of them is out helping children.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a lollipop man holds a round stop sign to see children across the road near schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A school crossing patrol helps children cross the road outside school.

clue.text: Girl catching banal ceremony before the end

indicators.note: catching means the girl's word holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a lass is a girl
trite means banal, overused

explanation.surface: A girl gets caught up in a dull ritual before the finale.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacraments given to a dying person form a religious ceremony just before death.

clue.text: The Donald bound to spoil rule with violent actions

indicators.note: to spoil something is to ruin it, so these letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Donald Trump is certain to spoil the rule of law with violence.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of THE DONALD BOUND gives BLOODANDTHUNDE; the R closes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood and thunder describes melodramatic violence and sensational action, as in pulp fiction.

clue.text: Person missing shot nets during a competition

indicators.note: during says the rearranged nets come in the middle of the competition

parts.note: a bee is a competition, as in a spelling bee

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of nets are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer is absent after a goal hits the nets during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone who is not present, missing from work or school.

clue.text: See 9
Lists including motorway as place to race

indicators.note: including means the word for lists takes the motorway inside

parts.note: a ship lists when it leans to one side
M is a motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Lists of roads including a motorway, where cars might race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lists' looks like a noun; it is the verb for tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: The French town hosts the famous 24-hour motor race, a venue for racing.

clue.text: Snoop around a Kardashian exhibiting flesh

indicators.note: around says the snoop surrounds the celebrity's name

parts.note: to snoop is to spy
Kim Kardashian is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Paparazzi snooping around a revealing Kardashian.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing is scanty and reveals a lot of skin.

clue.text: Love writer accessible to everyone

parts.note: love is zero, the letter O
a pen is a writer, something that writes

explanation.surface: A romantic novelist whose work everyone can enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: An open event or place is available to all, with nobody excluded.

clue.text: Vote Conservative? Crikey! Make sure that's right

parts.note: a cross is the mark made when voting
heck and crikey are both mild exclamations

explanation.surface: A voter is startled to back the Tories and double-checks the ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify something by checking it a second way is to confirm it is correct.

clue.text: Maybe Rod Stewart's tips to get groove

indicators.note: tips are a word's two ends, the first and last letters of the singer's surname

parts.note: a rut is a groove

explanation.surface: Rod Stewart's advice on getting into the groove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like the singer's first name; it is the definition, a rod being an example of a strut.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a bar or rod used as a structural brace, so a rod may be one.

clue.text: Turned up a shortened Madame Bovary?

definitions.text: Turned up a shortened Madame Bovary?

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: Mme is the short form of Madame

explanation.surface: Flaubert's heroine appears, compressed and upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is the clue's first part; the whole clue describes Flaubert's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's adulterous heroine has the first name Emma.

clue.text: Moment to change clothes for bit of pilot's kit

indicators.note: clothes means dresses or covers, so the word for change wraps around the moment

parts.note: to alter is to change
a moment is a time

explanation.surface: A pilot has a moment to change clothes before taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun; it is the verb, wrapping one word around another.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots use an instrument measuring height above sea level, part of a cockpit's equipment.

clue.text: Field team from Spain in the first half

indicators.note: in the first half means only the front half of the club's name is used

parts.note: Real Madrid is a Spanish football team

explanation.surface: A Spanish football side dominates the first half of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' looks like a pitch; it means an area of activity or knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity is a domain or sphere, which is a realm.

clue.text: River birds: they provide songs

parts.note: the Dee is a British river
jays are birds of the crow family

explanation.surface: Riverside birds singing for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They provide songs' looks like the birds; it is disc jockeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Disc jockeys play records on the radio or in clubs, supplying music.

clue.text: Leftist who's gently run media empire

parts.note: to trot is to run at a gentle pace
Sky is a broadcasting and media empire

explanation.surface: A left-winger who runs a media empire in a relaxed way.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was a Russian Marxist revolutionary, a figure of the far left.
